# Patient Intake and Scheduling Agent — Production Runbook

> **Scenario**: Patient Intake and Scheduling Agent
> **Platform**: Microsoft Copilot Studio — GitHub Copilot harness
> **Target readers**: Makers, delivery engineers, customer or partner operators

**Estimated effort**: Not yet measured; record actual effort on the Frontier Clock.

**Template:** an example to modify for your requirements; the customer or partner wires it into their environment. See the [Overview](1.Overview.md).

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build workload | 18 captured build checkpoints; 4 skills; 2 knowledge files; 5 acceptance checks; 4 locked cases. [Inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components), [checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks), and [cases](4.Sample-prompts.md#demo-prompts). | Template |
| Licensing and capacity | Confirm licensing for your tenant and Copilot Credits for the GitHub Copilot harness. Building, Preview and evaluation consume credits before publication. | Customer or partner |
| Environment and maker access | Record the approved patient-access environment, publisher prefix and maker access. Confirm the reviewed Sonnet46 model is available; keep the workshop synthetic and Draft. | Customer or partner |
| DLP and data policy | Have the administrator review uploaded intake files, proposed Dynamics 365 and SharePoint sources and the intended channel; document blocked paths rather than bypass them. | Customer or partner |
| Identity and audience | Review the supplied GroupMembership access policy, Integrated authentication and Always authentication trigger. Record who may build, test and later use the agent. | Customer or partner |
| Connection ownership | Name owners for the Dynamics 365 patient-access workflow and SharePoint governed intake documents. No customer connection is needed for the synthetic workshop. | Customer or partner |
| Test identities | Prepare front-desk, scheduling, patient-access and denied-access identities for an approved test deployment; makers use Draft Preview, not publication. | Customer or partner |
| Tooling by build lane | Manual lane: the Copilot Studio browser and reviewed files, with no PAC CLI or YAML import. Easy mode: VS Code Agent mode, the Microsoft Copilot Studio plugin and a supported PAC CLI. | Customer or partner |
| Privacy ownership | Have the privacy owner approve minimum-necessary fields and transcript handling before any patient data is used. | Customer or partner |

## Phase 0 — Qualify and Adapt the Template

### Step 0-1. Qualify the outcome and baseline

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Patient-access business owner

Complete the [qualification checklist](1.Overview.md#qualification-checklist).

**Measure:** Intake packet completeness, coverage follow-up, availability checks and pre-visit handoff consistency. Agree the starting readiness gaps before crediting any change to the agent.

Fill your baseline record:

| Visit type | Measurement period | Incomplete packets | Open coverage follow-ups | Handoff issues | Source system | Reviewer |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

Agree patient-access replacement connections, governance, support, telemetry and success measures before production.

### Step 0-2. Adapt scope and name owners

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Patient-access business owner

Adapt [scope](1.Overview.md#in-scope--out-of-scope) and the [data contract](2.Architecture.md#data-contract); assign approval roles.

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Patient-access business owner | Approve intake sources, scope and the review workflow; agree production success measures without treating synthetic records as results. |
| Qualified clinical and operational reviewers | Verify every substantive answer and own clinical, utilization, quality and operational decisions. |
| Authorized patient-access staff | Verify approved intake, payer, referral and scheduling systems before any action. |
| Copilot Studio maker | Build the reviewed instructions, two knowledge files and four skills; remove web search, confirm the model and keep the owned agent in Draft. |
| Power Platform administrator | Confirm tenant licensing and capacity, maker access, authenticated audience and data policies before any patient-access connection is approved. |
| Patient-access connection owners | Approve dedicated read-only references with no mutating actions for each approved patient-access source. |
| Acceptance reviewer | Check PI-01 through PI-04 and the boundary tests on the current Draft; fail any claim of a booking, authorization or record update. |
| Operations owner | Own production support, session and credit monitoring and configuration recovery; route patient decisions to authorized staff. |

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Patient-access replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures have named agreement.
- [ ] The patient-access owner records incomplete packets, late coverage follow-up and handoff gaps today before choosing measures.

## Phase 1 — Environment, Identity and Access

### Step 1-1. Approve the identity and settings design

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Review and approve the [identity design](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions) and [template settings](../../solutions/patient-intake/copilot-studio/settings.mcs.yml). Apply agent-specific settings when the agent is built in [Phase 2](#phase-2--build-and-prove-the-agent).

Approve document, connector and channel policies; require authentication and verify blocked routes stay blocked.

### Step 1-2. Configure tenant controls

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Approve the environment, audience and connection identities. Define the [authentication plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication); configure environment [data policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-data-loss-prevention).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The target environment and publisher prefix are approved before any build lane starts.
- [ ] The customer confirms an authenticated staff audience and minimum-necessary access to patient data.

## Phase 2 — Build and Prove the Agent

### Step 2-1. Choose the build lane

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

| Lane | Suits | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy mode with GitHub Copilot (default) | Assisted authoring | Synthetic Draft proof |
| Manual build in Copilot Studio | Browser-only makers | Same Draft proof |
| AIBAST Frontier (experimental) | Portable learning | Behavior proof; native validation follows |

[Compare lanes](1.Overview.md#delivery-lanes); local Brainstem remains optional.

### Step 2-2. Build the selected implementation

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

**Easy mode:** use the [authoring skill](../../skills/aibast-easy-mode-copilot/SKILL.md) and [reviewed messages](../../solutions/patient-intake/EASY-MODE-COPILOT-CHAT.md). **Manual:** use the [single inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components) and [tutorial](https://microsoft.github.io/aibast-agents-library/solutions/patient-intake/manual-tutorial.html) with the checklist below. **Portable learning:** follow [deployment.json](../../solutions/patient-intake/deployment.json); it does not replace native Draft validation.

**Manual build checklist** — [captured sequence](../../solutions/patient-intake/screenshots/manual/browserfilm.json). Record current results.

1. Create a blank Copilot Studio agent
2. Name Patient Intake Manual
3. Enter the reviewed global instructions
4. Save the instruction policy
5. Remove default web search
6. Add knowledge: aibast_patient-intake-review-rules.md
7. Add knowledge: aibast_patient-intake-synthetic-records.md
8. Add skill: appointment-availability
9. Add skill: coverage-evidence
10. Add skill: intake-readiness
11. Add skill: pre-visit-summary
12. Review model, skills, knowledge, and safety boundaries
13. Open a fresh Preview conversation
14. Pass PI-01: Front Desk Staff
15. Pass PI-02: Patient Access Representative
16. Pass PI-03: Scheduling Coordinator
17. Pass PI-04: Front Desk Staff
18. Confirm Draft and stop before publish

### Step 2-3. Enforce workshop integrity

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Apply the [workshop integrity and recovery rules](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) before replay.

### Step 2-4. Replay the synthetic proof

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

**Synthetic demo acceptance:** record every locked case: PI-01, PI-02, PI-03, PI-04. Use the [acceptance matrix](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [template acceptance checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] This lane's Preview evidence identifies the agent, environment, model, inventory, cases and Draft state.
- [ ] If this lane is chosen, the recipe smoke test calls `PatientIntakeAgent` and returns its required markers.
- [ ] The optional Brainstem lane is recorded as used or skipped; no workshop step depends on it.
- [ ] The manual build has reviewed instructions, two knowledge files, four skills and the confirmed model; web search and tools are absent.
- [ ] Each unchanged intake prompt passes once in a separate fresh Preview conversation on the owned Draft.
- [ ] The deterministic validator judges each full response; annotated screenshots do not replace the machine gate.
- [ ] Any Easy/Manual comparison uses identical instructions, knowledge, skills, model and case identifiers.

## Phase 3 — Wire In Your Systems

<a id="shared-integration-controls"></a>

**Shared identity and scope controls**

For each integration, decide end-user versus approved maker/service credentials. [Configure authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication) for the [authorized audience](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions).

**Shared scope:** Require sign-in before showing any patient information. Request only read scopes for minimum-necessary intake, coverage and scheduling fields. Restrict the audience and verify access with authorized and denied identities. Enforce these restrictions at each connection.

### Step 3-1. Integrate Dynamics 365 patient-access workflow

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Patient-access connection owners

1. **Bind Dynamics 365 patient-access workflow — read:** Bind dedicated read-only connector actions.

2. **Identity for Dynamics 365 patient-access workflow:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Dynamics 365 patient-access workflow:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Dynamics 365 patient-access workflow:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 1](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Determine no eligibility; transcribe the recorded evidence and the payer-portal follow-up. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim verified coverage, a booking or a record change.

### Step 3-2. Integrate SharePoint governed intake documents

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Patient-access connection owners

1. **Bind SharePoint governed intake documents — read:** Add governed document libraries as approved knowledge with a content owner.

2. **Identity for SharePoint governed intake documents:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope SharePoint governed intake documents:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for SharePoint governed intake documents:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 2](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Book or hold nothing; list candidate slots and state that nothing has been reserved or booked. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim verified coverage, a booking or a record change.

### Step 3-3. Integrate Approved payer and referral source systems

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Patient-access connection owners

1. **Bind Approved payer and referral source systems — read:** Bind least-privilege read-only actions.

2. **Identity for Approved payer and referral source systems:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Approved payer and referral source systems:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Approved payer and referral source systems:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 1](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Determine no eligibility; transcribe the recorded evidence and the payer-portal follow-up. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim verified coverage, a booking or a record change.

### Step 3-4. Integrate Approved scheduling system

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Patient-access connection owners

1. **Bind Approved scheduling system — read-write:** Start read-only; gate any hold or booking behind staff approval (preview).

2. **Identity for Approved scheduling system:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Approved scheduling system:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Approved scheduling system:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 2](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Book or hold nothing; list candidate slots and state that nothing has been reserved or booked. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim verified coverage, a booking or a record change.

### Step 3-5. Integrate Microsoft Teams staff approvals

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Patient-access connection owners

1. **Bind Microsoft Teams staff approvals — write:** Gate any approval request behind an authorized workflow (preview).

2. **Identity for Microsoft Teams staff approvals:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Microsoft Teams staff approvals:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Microsoft Teams staff approvals:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 3](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Send no reminder or message; route the request to an authorized human. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim verified coverage, a booking or a record change.

### Step 3-6. Connect

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Patient-access connection owners

Create and verify dedicated read-only references for the approved patient-access sources, with no mutating actions.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Dedicated read-only connection references are created and verified, with no mutating actions.
- [ ] No scheduling, outreach, submission, clinical-order or record-write action is configured.

## Phase 4 — Evaluate on Your Data

### Step 4-1. Adapt the evaluation corpus

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Preserve [locked behaviors](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [boundary tests](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases) when substituting approved customer fixtures.

### Step 4-2. Set thresholds and evaluate your data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Have the business owner approve thresholds. Run [adapted evaluations (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-agent-evaluation-intro) before publication under approved test user profiles. Keep exact assertions separate from General quality scores.

Before rollout, test an approved test deployment as front-desk, scheduling and patient-access users and an unshared identity; maker access does not prove user access.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The business owner sets customer-data measures; fictional records and slots are not current eligibility, appointment or clinical data.
- [ ] Adapted evaluations record the tested version and user profile; General quality scoring does not replace exact assertions.

## Phase 5 — Pilot and Rollout

### Step 5-1. Review the template release prerequisites

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

These synthetic regression gates do not set production thresholds. The reference workshop stays Draft; production approval belongs to the customer pilot.

| Template gate | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Locked intake corpus | All four cases, PI-01 through PI-04, satisfy every required and forbidden marker. |
| Manual inventory | Two knowledge files, four skills and the reviewed model; no tools or web search. |
| Healthcare boundary | Any diagnosis, treatment, eligibility or authorization outcome, scheduling, outreach, submission or record write is no-go. |
| Visual checkpoint acceptance | Require a positive target-state anchor without a blocker or refusal; withhold reshoot-required images. |
| Release state | The owned workshop agent is Draft with `published: false`. |

### Step 5-2. Publish and share deliberately

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Patient-access business owner

With business approval, [publish and share](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent) the adapted build with a restricted test audience. Keep the reference workshop Draft.

Require explicit confirmation before the production publish operation.

### Step 5-3. Run the governed pilot

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Patient-access business owner

**Pilot entry gate:** Test allowed and denied identities on the published, shared agent; resolve access failures before admitting pilot users. Compare pilot results with the baseline and thresholds; broaden rollout only after go/no-go.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The production publish operation has explicit human confirmation.
- [ ] The approved staff audience and supported channels are tested before publication is confirmed.

## Phase 6 — Operate

### Step 6-1. Retain the operational playbook

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Operations owner

The template provides the [state-and-recovery playbook](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) and regression cases.

### Step 6-2. Own changes and ongoing verification

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Operations owner

Review content freshness and permissions; re-evaluate source, model, skill or connector changes. [Monitor the deployed agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-overview).

Review failed intake sessions, their transcripts, tool connection and authentication errors, and credit use in Monitor.

### Step 6-3. Release: ALM

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

Back up the reviewed workspace, pull before editing and pushing, then package with `pac copilot pack`.

### Step 6-4. Release: recovery

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Confirm backup eligibility for the environment type and rehearse restoration to a supported test target.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The recovery rehearsal uses a restore path supported for the environment type and target.
- [ ] The operator reviews failed sessions, source usage, connection errors and credit consumption after rollout.

## Deliverables Checklist

### Template provides

- [ ] Agent, synthetic data and component inventory.
- [ ] Integration/identity contracts and evaluation cases.
- [ ] Build-to-operate playbooks and integrity rules.

### Customer or partner delivers

- [ ] Adapted mappings, identities, governance and connections.
- [ ] Customer-data results, thresholds and go/no-go.
- [ ] Approved publication, operations and recovery.
